    {
      "id": "WLOG02",
      "title": "Domain-member workstation: online AD DS password logon",
      "goal": "Connect local Windows sign-in to actual Kerberos AS/TGS work, local workstation service-ticket validation, and locally created access tokens.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: user",
        "L: Winlogon/LogonUI and credential provider",
        "A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role",
        "P: user process/session and kernel token role",
        "K: AD DS KDC/account database",
        "M: workstation machine credential and local Kerberos acceptor"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "WORKSTATION is an ADDS member; CORP\\alice exists; DC/DNS/time and machine relationship work.",
        "Select AES password preauthentication; no NTLM fallback in this fixture; FAST disabled only to isolate WLOG06.",
        "Pin current supported Windows11 client, Server2025 KDC, policy and complete MS-KILE revision; logical roles are not separate external servers."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "input",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Collect explicitly scoped CORP\\alice input and submit to the local Kerberos authentication package.",
          "artifacts": [
            "credential-input",
            "logon-request"
          ],
          "boundary": "LSASS submission is not a network request."
        },
        {
          "id": "as",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "K",
          "type": "network-exchange",
          "action": "Run existing AS request/reply model, including selected preauth metadata, client-derived key and KDC-owned authoritative key.",
          "artifacts": [
            "AS-REQ",
            "AS-REP",
            "user-account-key",
            "KDC-user-key",
            "opaque-TGT"
          ],
          "boundary": "No clear password crosses the KDC leg."
        },
        {
          "id": "as-accept",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "A",
          "type": "local-verify",
          "action": "Decrypt and validate the client part before acquiring the issued TGT session key and installing the opaque TGT.",
          "artifacts": [
            "accepted-TGT-credential"
          ],
          "boundary": "Ticket receipt is distinct from usable credential acquisition."
        },
        {
          "id": "host-ticket",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "K",
          "type": "network-exchange",
          "action": "Request host/workstation.corp.example for the workstation itself and validate its TGS reply.",
          "artifacts": [
            "host-TGS-REQ",
            "host-ticket",
            "host-session-key"
          ],
          "boundary": "Do not stop the sign-in explanation at receiving a TGT."
        },
        {
          "id": "local-ticket-check",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "M",
          "type": "local-call",
          "action": "The workstation Kerberos runtime interprets its host ticket and validated authorization data using its own service identity.",
          "artifacts": [
            "host-ticket",
            "validated-logon-information"
          ],
          "boundary": "This is local workstation processing, not a fabricated network AP exchange to another host."
        },
        {
          "id": "token",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-create",
          "action": "Combine validated domain identity/group information with local policy/alias membership and logon rights; create the primary token and start the session.",
          "artifacts": [
            "domain-SID",
            "group-SID-set",
            "local-policy",
            "primary-token",
            "desktop-session"
          ],
          "boundary": "Token issued locally, not sent by KDC."
        },
        {
          "id": "network-boundary",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "teaching-link",
          "action": "Offer a separate network-resource lesson using the retained credential context.",
          "artifacts": [
            "credential-context-reference"
          ],
          "boundary": "Desktop success does not authorize a share/file."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "wrong-password",
          "detector": "K",
          "condition": "Preauthentication fails",
          "stopBoundary": "as",
          "preserved": "No accepted user TGT or local token."
        },
        {
          "id": "clock-or-spn",
          "detector": "K/A",
          "condition": "Time or workstation service target invalid",
          "stopBoundary": "as or host-ticket",
          "preserved": "No invented local success; retain prior valid credential history where applicable."
        },
        {
          "id": "host-key-mismatch",
          "detector": "M",
          "condition": "Ticket cannot be accepted by the selected machine identity",
          "stopBoundary": "local-ticket-check",
          "preserved": "TGT receipt is not a desktop grant."
        },
        {
          "id": "denied-local-logon",
          "detector": "A",
          "condition": "Domain authentication succeeds but local deny right applies",
          "stopBoundary": "token",
          "preserved": "No usable desktop; no arbitrary cached bypass."
        },
        {
          "id": "password-change-required",
          "detector": "K",
          "condition": "Account requires change before authentication completes",
          "stopBoundary": "as",
          "preserved": "Explicit stop/cross-link; do not invent an inline password-change protocol."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Assert AS/TGS target, key owner, reply receipt/acceptance and local-token boundaries.",
        "No domain password transmitted to SAM, no SAM verifier masquerading as an AES key, and no user token copied out of a TGT.",
        "Token provenance lists domain identity/group facts separately from local aliases/privileges and application access decisions.",
        "Do not teach arbitrary Kerberos-error-to-NTLM fallback; a future compatibility branch needs its own sourced condition and carrier."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "user/KDC AES handles",
        "AS client part/TGT/TGT key",
        "host ticket/key",
        "validated PAC/logon data",
        "local group/policy facts",
        "token",
        "profile/session"
      ],
      "crossLinks": [
        "Existing standalone ADDS/password lessons",
        "lab-smb-nonjoined-kerberos"
      ],

    {
      "id": "WLOG03",
      "title": "Domain member, explicit local account: same name, different SID",
      "goal": "Explain why .\\alice, WORKSTATION\\alice and CORP\\alice can select different authorities and do not become the same principal because their names match.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: user",
        "L: Winlogon/LogonUI and credential provider",
        "A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role",
        "P: user process/session and kernel token role",
        "S: local SAM authority",
        "K: ADDS authority shown as uncontacted"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Machine is a domain member; both local alice and domain alice exist with deliberately different SIDs/password fixtures.",
        "Select .\\alice explicitly; no account-name guessing or silent authority fallback."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "scope",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Choose the local account and show normalized authority WORKSTATION before submitting the password.",
          "artifacts": [
            "account-scope"
          ],
          "boundary": "Displayed name alone is not the identity."
        },
        {
          "id": "sam",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "S",

            "local-verifier",
            "local-validation"

        },
        {
          "id": "token",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "P",

          "from": "P",

    {
      "id": "WLOG04",
      "title": "Offline domain logon: cached local verifier, no fresh KDC grant",
      "goal": "Demonstrate a previously signed-in domain user entering a disconnected desktop and distinguish cached validation from fresh domain authentication and network credentials.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: user",
        "L: Winlogon/LogonUI and credential provider",
        "A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role",
        "P: user process/session and kernel token role",
        "C: protected local cached-domain-logon store",
        "K: unavailable domain controller"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Domain member with a prior successful online password sign-in for CORP\\alice and an explicitly enabled cache policy.",
        "DC is unreachable, not actively rejecting the presented credential; user is not Protected Users.",
        "New boot/session fixture has no reusable live TGT; model cached verifier symbolically, not as a recoverable password or pass-the-hash credential."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "attempt",
          "from": "L",
          "to": "A",
          "type": "local-call",
          "action": "Submit domain-scoped input; establish that the selected online authority is unavailable.",
          "artifacts": [
            "logon-request",
            "availability-result"
          ],
          "boundary": "Timeout/unreachable result is not an account-validation response."
        },
        {
          "id": "cache-policy",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "C",
          "type": "local-check",
          "action": "Check cache policy and locate this user prior verifier/account-information entry.",
          "artifacts": [
            "cache-policy",
            "cached-verifier",
            "cached-account-data"
          ],
          "boundary": "Cache availability is explicit preexisting state."
        },
        {
          "id": "verify",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "A",
          "type": "local-verify",
          "action": "Validate current input locally against the cached verifier.",
          "artifacts": [
            "cached-validation-result"
          ],
          "boundary": "No KDC learns or grants anything."
        },
        {
          "id": "session",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-create",
          "action": "Apply effective local logon policy and create the locally authorized token/desktop using the declared cached identity snapshot.",
          "artifacts": [
            "cached-identity-snapshot",
            "primary-token",
            "desktop"
          ],
          "boundary": "Offline success cannot imply fresh remote group/account-state knowledge."
        },
        {
          "id": "resource",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "teaching-link",
          "action": "Show later network authentication as a separate attempt that still needs a reachable authority/valid usable credential.",
          "artifacts": [
            "network-attempt-state"
          ],
          "boundary": "The cache entry itself is never a wire credential."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "no-cache",
          "detector": "C",
          "condition": "First use of this domain account, entry evicted, or cache disabled",
          "stopBoundary": "cache-policy",
          "preserved": "No offline desktop."
        },
        {
          "id": "cache-mismatch",
          "detector": "A",
          "condition": "Input does not match the existing verifier",
          "stopBoundary": "verify",
          "preserved": "No success."
        },
        {
          "id": "protected-user",
          "detector": "C",
          "condition": "Protected Users rules prevented cache-verifier creation",
          "stopBoundary": "cache-policy",
          "preserved": "Explain policy reason without changing the account policy."
        },
        {
          "id": "online-rejection",
          "detector": "K",
          "condition": "DC reachable and rejects this credential/account",
          "stopBoundary": "attempt",
          "preserved": "Do not bypass the rejection with a stale cache."
        },
        {
          "id": "stale-password-or-disable",
          "detector": "A",
          "condition": "DC-side change is unknown offline",
          "stopBoundary": "session",
          "preserved": "Label local/stale verification explicitly; no claim of fresh domain approval."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Wire inventory contains no transmitted cache verifier, password derived from cache, fresh AS-REP or fresh domain status.",
        "Positive offline case has zero new KDC-issued tickets.",
        "Preserve the difference between new input credentials, cached verifier and any later LSA credential handle.",
        "Cite/pin cache and Protected Users policy instead of teaching cached logon as universally available."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "cache policy/verifier/account snapshot",
        "availability result",
        "local validation",
        "local token/session",
        "network-attempt placeholder"
      ],
      "crossLinks": [
        "WLOG02",
        "WLOG07"
      ],
      "researchGates": [],
      "sources": [
        {
          "id": "W-S08",

          "url": "https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/user-profiles-and-logon/cached-domain-logon-information",
          "sections": "CachedLogonsCount and disconnected logon",

    {
      "id": "WLOG05",
      "title": "Smart-card domain sign-in: local PIN and PKINIT to desktop",
      "goal": "Connect card-local private-key authorization to PKINIT, current certificate mapping, a local workstation ticket and Windows session creation.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: user",
        "L: Winlogon/LogonUI and credential provider",
        "A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role",
        "P: user process/session and kernel token role",
        "T: smart card and CSP/KSP role",
        "K: ADDS KDC",
        "M: workstation Kerberos acceptor"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Domain member; provisioned nonexportable card key/certificate, KDC certificate/trust and strong account binding.",
        "Use accepted AD03 fresh-DH reference; pin current MS-PKCA24.0 Windows algorithm/freshness profile before product-specific claims.",
        "Certificate provisioning is preexisting; online CA issuance is not a login message."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "select",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Select a permitted certificate tile; collect PIN into the protected local credential pipeline.",
          "artifacts": [
            "certificate",
            "protected-PIN-input",
            "card-key-handle"
          ],
          "boundary": "PIN is not an AD password or KDC padata value."
        },
        {
          "id": "sign",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "T",
          "type": "local-call",
          "action": "Authorize the card operation and sign the PKINIT request with the card-resident key.",
          "artifacts": [
            "signed-AuthPack",
            "card-key-handle"
          ],
          "boundary": "Only signature/public certificate leave the card boundary."
        },
        {
          "id": "pkinit",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "K",
          "type": "network-exchange",
          "action": "Reuse the accepted PKINIT request/DH reply sequence and current certificate-chain, EKU, revocation and strong mapping checks.",
          "artifacts": [
            "PA-PK-AS-REQ",
            "PA-PK-AS-REP",
            "DH/reply-key-context"
          ],
          "boundary": "UPN-only weak mapping is not the modern happy path."
        },
        {
          "id": "accept",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "A",
          "type": "local-verify",
          "action": "Validate KDC proof, nonce and reply; acquire the distinct issued user TGT/session key.",
          "artifacts": [
            "TGT-credential"
          ],
          "boundary": "No desktop grant at AS packet receipt."
        },
        {
          "id": "host",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "M",
          "type": "teaching-macro",
          "action": "Run the WLOG02 host/workstation TGS and local validation boundaries using this acquired credential.",
          "artifacts": [
            "host-ticket",
            "validated-domain-logon-data"
          ],
          "boundary": "Macro expands to the existing actual events, not one invented PDU."
        },
        {
          "id": "desktop",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-create",
          "action": "Apply local logon rights and create the local token/session; release temporary PIN input.",
          "artifacts": [
            "token",
            "desktop",
            "PIN-cleanup"
          ],
          "boundary": "Card removal/lock policy is a later action."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "bad-pin",
          "detector": "T",
          "condition": "Card rejects PIN/private-key authorization",
          "stopBoundary": "sign",
          "preserved": "No signed request or KDC contact for this attempt."
        },
        {
          "id": "weak-mapping",
          "detector": "K",
          "condition": "Trusted certificate cannot be strongly bound to account",
          "stopBoundary": "pkinit",
          "preserved": "No accepted TGT despite certificate trust."
        },
        {
          "id": "invalid-user-cert",
          "detector": "K",
          "condition": "Selected validity/revocation/trust check fails",
          "stopBoundary": "pkinit",
          "preserved": "Detector and returned error kept distinct."
        },
        {
          "id": "invalid-kdc-proof",
          "detector": "A",
          "condition": "Client rejects KDC certificate/signature/DH reply",
          "stopBoundary": "accept",
          "preserved": "No accepted credential."
        },
        {
          "id": "card-removed",
          "detector": "T",
          "condition": "Card unavailable before the required operation completes",
          "stopBoundary": "sign",
          "preserved": "No successful operation fabricated."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "PIN and private-key custody remain local; card-key never readable at KDC or process.",
        "Strong-binding rejection differs from signature validity and local logon-right denial.",
        "Reuse AD03 verified key distinctions instead of new simplified PKINIT code.",
        "No unconditional password credential appears after certificate logon."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "PIN input/cleanup",
        "card private-key handle",
        "public cert/chain",
        "signed AuthPack",
        "DH secret/reply key",
        "TGT/key",
        "host ticket",
        "token/session"
      ],
      "crossLinks": [
        "lab-ad-pkinit-success",
        "lab-ad-pkinit-binding",
        "WLOG02"
      ],
      "researchGates": [
        "Offline smart-card logon and PKINIT+FAST composition require separately sourced/platform-pinned branches; do not infer their internals from password-cache or standalone FAST."
      ],
      "sources": [
        {

    {
      "id": "WLOG06",
      "title": "Domain password sign-in with required FAST armor",
      "goal": "Make computer authentication, user authentication and local Windows session creation separate stages when Kerberos armoring is required.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: user",
        "L: Winlogon/LogonUI and credential provider",
        "A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role",
        "P: user process/session and kernel token role",
        "M: machine Kerberos credential context",
        "K: FAST-capable ADDS KDC"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Domain member; client armoring enabled, RequireFAST=true, compatible realm/DC and usable computer TGT.",
        "Use accepted AD04 PA-ENCRYPTED-CHALLENGE and reply-strengthening model; user and computer identities/keys differ."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "armor-ready",
          "from": "M",
          "to": "M",
          "type": "local-check",
          "action": "Validate machine armor credential availability, realm capability and selected client/KDC policy.",
          "artifacts": [
            "computer-TGT",
            "computer-session-key",
            "FAST-policy"
          ],
          "boundary": "A machine TGT is not Alice authentication."
        },
        {
          "id": "user-request",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "K",
          "type": "network-exchange",
          "action": "Reuse AD04 explicit-armored user AS request with protected challenge and request checksum.",
          "artifacts": [
            "armor-AP-REQ",
            "armor-key",
            "FAST-request",
            "user-challenge"
          ],
          "boundary": "No substitution of armor key for user long-term key."
        },
        {
          "id": "kdc",
          "from": "K",
          "to": "K",
          "type": "local-verify",
          "action": "Verify armor and inner user authentication separately, then form protected response and required strengthened reply key.",
          "artifacts": [
            "FAST-reply",
            "strengthen-key",
            "user-TGT"
          ],
          "boundary": "Armor acceptance alone does not issue a user credential."
        },
        {
          "id": "accept",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "A",
          "type": "local-verify",
          "action": "Validate finished/bindings and decrypt the AS reply before installing the user TGT/key.",
          "artifacts": [
            "accepted-user-TGT"
          ],
          "boundary": "Receipt/unwrap/acceptance remain explicit."
        },
        {
          "id": "desktop",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "teaching-macro",
          "action": "Continue host-workstation TGS/local validation and policy/token stages from WLOG02.",
          "artifacts": [
            "host-ticket",
            "logon-data",
            "token/session"
          ],
          "boundary": "FAST protects AS/TGS, not every subsequent application message."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "armor-missing",
          "detector": "M/A",
          "condition": "Required computer TGT unavailable",
          "stopBoundary": "armor-ready",
          "preserved": "No user TGT or unadvertised unarmored fallback."
        },
        {
          "id": "realm-or-dc-unsupported",
          "detector": "A",
          "condition": "Required support absent",
          "stopBoundary": "armor-ready",
          "preserved": "Fail required profile; optional fallback belongs to named AD04 variant."
        },
        {
          "id": "tampered-fast",
          "detector": "K/A",
          "condition": "Bad armor/checksum/protected response",
          "stopBoundary": "kdc or accept",
          "preserved": "No usable user credential."
        },
        {
          "id": "bad-user-proof",
          "detector": "K",
          "condition": "Valid armor but user authentication fails",
          "stopBoundary": "kdc",
          "preserved": "Machine identity acceptance preserved, user denied."
        },
        {
          "id": "bootstrap",
          "detector": "M",
          "condition": "Machine has no TGT",
          "stopBoundary": "armor-ready",
          "preserved": "Link existing computer-bootstrap exception; do not demand machine armor recursively."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Reuse exact AD04 operation/key history and its corrected reply strengthening.",
        "Separate machine TGT, armor key, user long-term key, strengthened reply key and issued user TGT key.",
        "Profile explains why required FAST differs from opportunistic fallback."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "machine credential",
        "armoring policy/support evidence",
        "armor key",
        "protected challenge",
        "strengthen/reply keys",
        "user TGT",
        "local token"
      ],
      "crossLinks": [
        "lab-ad-fast-as-success",
        "lab-ad-fast-as-bootstrap",
        "lab-ad-fast-as-optional-fallback",
        "WLOG02"
      ],

    {
      "id": "WLOG07",
      "title": "Unlock an existing Windows session: local and domain policy branches",
      "goal": "Show reauthentication to unlock an existing desktop without turning lock/unlock into logoff/new-session creation.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: user",
        "L: Winlogon/LogonUI and credential provider",
        "A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role",
        "P: user process/session and kernel token role",
        "C: local unlock/cached validation role",
        "K: domain controller when required"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "An existing workstation session, processes, token handles and locked desktop are seeded.",
        "Base: local password account. Named domain profiles pin both RequireDomainControllerAuthenticationToUnlock and cache policy."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "lock",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-state",
          "action": "Lock interactive access while retaining the existing processes/session and token identities.",
          "artifacts": [
            "locked-session",
            "existing-token"
          ],
          "boundary": "Lock is not logoff or token destruction."
        },
        {
          "id": "input",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Collect credential for the locked-session identity and dispatch the declared unlock path.",
          "artifacts": [
            "unlock-request"
          ],
          "boundary": "A different user belongs to switch-user/new logon, not this unlock."
        },
        {
          "id": "policy",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "A",
          "type": "local-check",
          "action": "Select local validation, domain cached validation or required DC reauthentication from explicit policy.",
          "artifacts": [
            "unlock-policy",
            "cache-policy"
          ],
          "boundary": "UI shows what authority is actually consulted."
        },
        {
          "id": "verify",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "C/K",
          "type": "local-or-network",
          "action": "Perform only the selected verification branch; label cached facts as potentially stale.",
          "artifacts": [
            "unlock-validation-result"
          ],
          "boundary": "An unavailable DC cannot magically return authentication success."
        },
        {
          "id": "resume",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-state",
          "action": "Permit access to the same session after successful verification; release attempt input.",
          "artifacts": [
            "existing-session-reference",
            "input-cleanup"
          ],
          "boundary": "Desktop identity and prior process token handles remain attributable."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "bad-credential",
          "detector": "C/K",
          "condition": "Selected verifier rejects input",
          "stopBoundary": "verify",
          "preserved": "Session stays locked; existing processes/tokens remain."
        },
        {
          "id": "required-dc-unavailable",
          "detector": "A",
          "condition": "Require DC enabled and selected cache policy disallows local substitute",
          "stopBoundary": "verify",
          "preserved": "Stay locked."
        },
        {
          "id": "cached-domain-change",
          "detector": "C",
          "condition": "Domain disable/group change not observed by cached unlock",
          "stopBoundary": "verify",
          "preserved": "Label stale knowledge; do not refresh existing process groups from nowhere."
        },
        {
          "id": "other-user",
          "detector": "L",
          "condition": "Different identity selected",
          "stopBoundary": "input",
          "preserved": "Cross-link new logon/switch-user; never overwrite the locked session."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Session/process/token identifiers match before lock and after successful unlock.",
        "Failed unlock changes attempt state, not existing session legitimacy.",
        "Domain-required and cached-unlock profiles have different real actor/message inventories.",
        "Do not use deprecated LogonUser LOGON32_LOGON_UNLOCK as a fabricated universal modern API sequence; use supported unlock structures/source or label internal dispatch abstract."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "existing session/token/process references",
        "lock state",
        "unlock policy",
        "verification attempt",
        "cleanup"
      ],
      "crossLinks": [
        "WLOG01",
        "WLOG04"
      ],
      "researchGates": [
        "Offline smart-card/Hello unlock internals are not inferred; add only after credential-specific sourcing."
      ],
      "sources": [
        {

    {
      "id": "WLOG08",
      "title": "Nonjoined PC: domain credentials do not replace the local desktop identity",
      "goal": "Answer the workgroup-workstation question directly: local console sign-in and explicit domain access to a member-server share are different journeys.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: user",
        "L: Winlogon/LogonUI and credential provider",
        "A: LSA/LSASS authentication and policy role",
        "P: user process/session and kernel token role",
        "S: local SAM",
        "F: domain-member file server",
        "K: ADDS authority used only in the linked network flow"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "WORKGROUPPC is not joined; local bob account exists; no local alice account or preexisting domain interactive-logon relationship.",
        "Explicit domain network credentials belong to CORP\\alice; accepted SMB3.1.1 fixtures already exist."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "scope",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Show machine membership and available console account authority before the attempt.",
          "artifacts": [
            "membership",
            "console-authority"
          ],
          "boundary": "Typing CORP\\alice does not join the device or provision a local principal."
        },
        {
          "id": "console-deny",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-result",
          "action": "Reject the unsupported selected domain interactive-logon attempt in this workgroup profile.",
          "artifacts": [
            "console-failure"
          ],
          "boundary": "No domain token, desktop or cached-domain account is created."
        },
        {
          "id": "local-logon",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "teaching-macro",
          "action": "Run WLOG01 as WORKGROUPPC\\bob to obtain a local desktop.",
          "artifacts": [
            "local-token",
            "desktop"
          ],
          "boundary": "Local principal remains bob."
        },
        {
          "id": "network-input",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Enter CORP\\alice for one explicit network attempt or launch WELEV05 network-only context.",
          "artifacts": [
            "network-credential-handle"
          ],
          "boundary": "Credential submission is not validation."
        },
        {
          "id": "smb",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "F/K",
          "type": "teaching-link",
          "action": "Continue the already accepted SMB02 configured Kerberos journey; offer SMB01 only as explicitly labeled NTLMv2 compatibility.",
          "artifacts": [
            "SMB-session-reference"
          ],
          "boundary": "Share/file authorization and server-side identity remain separate."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "bad-network-password",
          "detector": "K",
          "condition": "Credential rejected in linked SMB04",
          "stopBoundary": "smb",
          "preserved": "Local bob desktop remains."
        },
        {
          "id": "no-kerberos-prerequisite",
          "detector": "P",
          "condition": "KDC/SPN/discovery unavailable for selected Kerberos profile",
          "stopBoundary": "smb",
          "preserved": "No implicit NTLM fallback just because device is nonjoined."
        },
        {
          "id": "resource-denial",
          "detector": "F",
          "condition": "Authenticated identity denied by share/file ACL",
          "stopBoundary": "smb",
          "preserved": "Local desktop and accepted SMB authentication history remain."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Cross-links open actual accepted SMB IDs; do not duplicate/rewrite the SMB implementation.",
        "Always display local SID/session and outbound account separately.",
        "No cached domain console success exists without the joined/prior-cache prerequisites of WLOG04.",
        "Do not claim a remote machine-local account authenticates the local workstation; remote account authority belongs to the target."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "join-state fact",
        "console-authority selection/failure",
        "local-token",
        "outbound credential handle",
        "remote session reference"
      ],
      "crossLinks": [

        "lab-smb-nonjoined-ntlm",
        "lab-smb-nonjoined-bad-credential",
        "lab-smb-nonjoined-share-denied",
        "lab-smb-nonjoined-file-denied",
        "WELEV05"

    {
      "id": "WELEV01",
      "title": "Administrator membership versus the process token actually used",
      "goal": "Explain classic UAC token filtering, group attributes, privileges and integrity before any elevation request.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: administrator user",
        "A: LSA/token policy",
        "P: Explorer and ordinary child process",
        "O: object access-check role"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Classic Admin Approval Mode explicitly selected; Administrator protection disabled for this reference.",
        "Named non-built-in administrator account, UAC enabled; SID membership and requested file operation fixed."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "token-pair",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "A",
          "type": "local-create",
          "action": "After successful sign-in, create the linked full and filtered token representations for the selected administrator.",
          "artifacts": [
            "full-token",
            "filtered-token",
            "linked-token-reference"
          ],
          "boundary": "Same account identity does not mean identical enabled groups/privileges."
        },
        {
          "id": "shell",
          "from": "A",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-create",
          "action": "Run Explorer and ordinary child with the filtered token at the selected medium integrity level.",
          "artifacts": [
            "process-token-reference"
          ],
          "boundary": "The full token is not the process active token."
        },
        {
          "id": "inspect",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-inspect",
          "action": "Compare user SID, group attributes, privileges/enabled flags, elevation type and integrity label.",
          "artifacts": [
            "token-field-view"
          ],
          "boundary": "Do not equate membership with an enabled authorization SID."
        },
        {
          "id": "access",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "O",
          "type": "local-check",
          "action": "Evaluate a declared protected operation using mandatory policy then DACL/privilege rules applicable to that operation.",
          "artifacts": [
            "object-integrity-label",
            "DACL",
            "decision"
          ],
          "boundary": "No automatic elevation merely because an operation is denied."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "filtered-admin-access",
          "detector": "O",
          "condition": "Filtered token lacks effective right for selected admin operation",
          "stopBoundary": "access",
          "preserved": "Process remains unelevated."
        },
        {
          "id": "high-integrity-still-denied",
          "detector": "O",
          "condition": "Comparison full token still fails an explicit DACL",
          "stopBoundary": "access",
          "preserved": "High integrity is not blanket allow."
        },
        {
          "id": "standard-user",
          "detector": "A",
          "condition": "Account has no administrator membership",
          "stopBoundary": "token-pair",
          "preserved": "One standard token; no invented linked full token."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Expose token differences as exact fields, including deny-only versus enabled SID attributes where pinned.",
        "Integrity check, discretionary access and privilege checks are separate concepts; do not imply a universal fixed order for every privilege-taking API.",
        "A token is an OS authorization object, not an OAuth token, password, ticket or remotely transferable credential."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "linked token pair",
        "group attributes",
        "privilege enabled flags",
        "integrity SID",
        "DACL/mandatory policy",
        "access decision"
      ],
      "crossLinks": [
        "WLOG01",
        "WLOG02",
        "WELEV02"
      ],
      "researchGates": [],
      "sources": [

    {
      "id": "WELEV02",
      "title": "Run as administrator: consent for the signed-in administrator",
      "goal": "Trace an explicit elevation request through AppInfo/secure-desktop consent to a new elevated process while preserving the original process.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: signed-in administrator",
        "P: unelevated caller",
        "B: AppInfo/elevation broker",
        "L: secure-desktop consent UI",
        "E: elevated process",
        "O: protected object"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Classic Admin Approval Mode; named administrator; consent-on-secure-desktop policy; no auto-elevation case.",
        "Explicit runas shell verb/requestedExecutionLevel requiresAdministrator on a synthetic harmless helper."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "request",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "B",
          "type": "local-call",
          "action": "Submit the selected executable/requested operation with caller identity.",
          "artifacts": [
            "elevation-request",
            "executable-identity"
          ],
          "boundary": "Request is neither user approval nor process elevation."
        },
        {
          "id": "prompt",
          "from": "B",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-ui",
          "action": "Evaluate policy and display publisher/path/operation in the secure-desktop consent prompt.",
          "artifacts": [
            "prompt-policy",
            "consent-challenge"
          ],
          "boundary": "No credential verification is invented for a consent-only branch."
        },
        {
          "id": "consent",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "L",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Approve this concrete request and return the decision to the broker.",
          "artifacts": [
            "consent-result"
          ],
          "boundary": "Consent is scoped to the pending request."
        },
        {
          "id": "launch",
          "from": "B",
          "to": "E",
          "type": "local-create",
          "action": "Create the new process with the available full administrator token at high integrity.",
          "artifacts": [
            "elevated-process",
            "full-token-reference"
          ],
          "boundary": "Do not mutate caller token or every other process."
        },
        {
          "id": "operation",
          "from": "E",
          "to": "O",
          "type": "local-check",
          "action": "Apply the selected object access/privilege check and return the real operation result.",
          "artifacts": [
            "operation-result"
          ],
          "boundary": "Elevation does not guarantee resource authorization."
        },
        {
          "id": "exit",
          "from": "E",
          "to": "E",
          "type": "local-cleanup",
          "action": "Release this process/token handle at exit; retain the signed-in session.",
          "artifacts": [
            "process-exit"
          ],
          "boundary": "No claim that classic linked admin token disappears globally."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "cancel",
          "detector": "U",
          "condition": "User declines/cancels",
          "stopBoundary": "consent",
          "preserved": "No elevated process; caller survives."
        },
        {
          "id": "policy-deny",
          "detector": "B",
          "condition": "Selected elevation policy disallows request",
          "stopBoundary": "prompt",
          "preserved": "No credential or consent accepted."
        },
        {
          "id": "launch-failure",
          "detector": "B",
          "condition": "Approved executable cannot start",
          "stopBoundary": "launch",
          "preserved": "Consent history remains; no running elevated process."
        },
        {
          "id": "operation-denied",
          "detector": "O",
          "condition": "Elevated process fails the selected ACL",
          "stopBoundary": "operation",
          "preserved": "Elevation remains historically successful."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Consented request and newly launched process are correlated.",
        "Consent-only branch has no new password, Kerberos AS or SAM verification event.",
        "Original process/session token remains unchanged through success/cancel."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "request/policy",
        "consent prompt/result",
        "caller/full-token references",
        "new process",
        "operation result",
        "exit"
      ],

        "WELEV01",
        "WELEV03"

    {
      "id": "WELEV03",
      "title": "Standard-user elevation: authenticate a separate administrator",
      "goal": "Show a credential prompt as authentication of the chosen administrator and creation of that account’s elevated process, not an upgrade to the original standard-user identity.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: standard desktop user",
        "V: credential-supplying administrator",
        "P: caller process",
        "B/L: elevation broker/secure prompt",
        "A: local LSA and selected account authority",
        "E: elevated process"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Classic Admin Approval Mode; standard-user policy prompts for credentials.",
        "Base administrator is WORKSTATION\\admin2 in local SAM; separately named domain-admin-credential variant requires domain reachability and applicable local membership/rights."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "request",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "B/L",
          "type": "local-call",
          "action": "Request elevation and present an administrator credential prompt with explicit account scope.",
          "artifacts": [
            "elevation-request",

      "id": "WELEV05",

      "goal": "Demonstrate NewCredentials without validating the entered domain password at launch; the first network attempt is where authentication succeeds or fails.",
      "tier": "core",
      "actors": [
        "U: local desktop user",
        "R: runas/Secondary Logon role",

        "P/Q: original/new local process",

        "K: domain authority"
      ],
      "preconditions": [

      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "input",

          "to": "R",

          ],
          "boundary": "This is not an interactive domain workstation logon."

        {
          "id": "context",
          "from": "R",
          "to": "A",

          "action": "Create the new LSA network-credential context and launch Q with the caller local security identity.",

          ],

        {

      "actors": [
        "U: signed-in administrator",

        "A: system-managed administrator identity/profile",
        "E: isolated elevated process"

      ],

    {
      "id": "WELEV07",
      "title": "Optional: sudo for Windows delegates elevation to UAC",
      "goal": "Explain the Windows command’s UAC-backed elevation and console modes without importing Unix sudoers/PAM semantics.",
      "tier": "optional",
      "actors": [
        "U: console user",
        "P: unelevated sudo client",
        "B: UAC/elevation service",
        "E: elevated command"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Optional follow-on after WELEV01–06; pin Windows11 24H2+ build and sudo version.",
        "Feature explicitly enabled; choose forceNewWindow for the base; named disableInput/normal modes only if demonstrated."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "invoke",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Enter a harmless predefined sudo command.",
          "artifacts": [
            "command",
            "sudo-mode"
          ],
          "boundary": "No Unix policy file or timestamp cache is invented."
        },
        {
          "id": "uac",
          "from": "P",
          "to": "B",
          "type": "local-call",
          "action": "Request platform UAC elevation using the effective Windows policy.",
          "artifacts": [
            "elevation-request"
          ],
          "boundary": "Windows sudo is not a replacement authentication protocol."
        },
        {
          "id": "approve",
          "from": "U",
          "to": "B",
          "type": "local-input",
          "action": "Complete the actual configured UAC prompt.",
          "artifacts": [
            "approval-result"
          ],
          "boundary": "Cancel produces no elevated command."
        },
        {
          "id": "launch",
          "from": "B",
          "to": "E",
          "type": "local-create",
          "action": "Start the command in the selected window/input mode with its accepted elevated context.",
          "artifacts": [
            "process",
            "token-reference",
            "stdio-mode"
          ],
          "boundary": "Changing console mode does not select an alternate account."
        },
        {
          "id": "exit",
          "from": "E",
          "to": "P",
          "type": "local-result",
          "action": "Return/close the selected command and release scoped handles.",
          "artifacts": [
            "exit-status"
          ],
          "boundary": "No persistent general-purpose admin grant."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        {
          "id": "disabled",
          "detector": "P",
          "condition": "sudo feature not enabled",
          "stopBoundary": "invoke",
          "preserved": "No implicit configuration change."
        },
        {
          "id": "uac-cancel",
          "detector": "B",
          "condition": "Prompt declined",
          "stopBoundary": "approve",
          "preserved": "No elevated command."
        },
        {
          "id": "other-user-option",
          "detector": "P",
          "condition": "Unsupported attempt to run as another user",
          "stopBoundary": "invoke",
          "preserved": "Cross-link runas; do not pretend sudo -u compatibility."
        }
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Label Windows sudo distinctly from Linux/macOS sudo lessons.",
        "forceNewWindow, disableInput and normal affect I/O coupling, not PAM/sudoers policy.",
        "Do not include this optional scenario in mandatory core acceptance count unless selected by root plan."
      ],
      "heldArtifacts": [
        "command/mode",
        "UAC request/result",
        "elevated process/token",
        "I/O handles",
        "exit status"
      ],
      "crossLinks": [
        "WELEV02",
        "WELEV04"
      ],

      "id": "LLOG01",
      "title": "Linux local workstation login through PAM",
      "goal": "Explain the local identity, authentication, account-policy and session boundaries using a declared PAM service stack.",
      "actors": [
        "Person",
        "Console login or display-manager service",
        "PAM stack",
        "Local identity/credential database",
        "Session manager/logind"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Profile L-PAM: one explicitly supplied service stack; local files identity and pam_unix password backend; no directory or KDC dependency.",
        "Select systemd session integration explicitly; do not imply every Linux login uses logind or the same stack ordering."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "Resolve the entered local account to UID, GID, groups, home and shell; label this identity lookup rather than proof of identity.",
        "Start the named PAM transaction and show the conversation delivering a secret only to the selected authentication module.",
        "Evaluate configured auth-stack control flow and the credential verdict.",
        "Run account checks separately; make account expiry or access denial visible after successful authentication.",
        "Establish credentials and open the session in the application profile; show pam_systemd registration only where configured, then the resulting process identity.",
        "Close the session and PAM transaction; discard transient secret/conversation state while preserving the account record."
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "Unknown user; incorrect password; authenticated account denied; session setup failure.",
        "A blank password is denied in the baseline. A nullok or passwordless account requires a separately labeled explicit configuration."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Auth success alone cannot create the desktop; account and session gates must be represented.",
        "Held objects distinguish identity record, verifier, transient entered secret and session handle; the application never receives the stored password verifier as a reusable login token.",
        "Local calls and filesystem accesses are not fake network packets. Basic and expert views use the same causal events."
      ],

      "id": "LELEV01",
      "title": "sudo: policy, authenticated identity and timestamp reuse",
      "goal": "Show who is requesting, whose identity is checked and which account executes the requested command.",

      ],

        "Determine authentication requirement from matching rule and valid timestamp scope.",
        "If required, run the configured PAM authentication for the selected identity; include account/session effects where configured.",
        "Write or refresh only the appropriate timestamp record after successful authentication.",

    {
      "id": "JWT01",
      "title": "JWT, JWS, JWE and opaque tokens",
      "goal": "Separate token representation from the protocol, protection and authorization decision.",
      "actors": [
        "Issuer",
        "Client",
        "Resource server"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Three fixed synthetic examples; no real credentials; compact serialization explicitly selected."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "number": 1,
          "phase": "issue",
          "action": "Create a signed three-segment JWT, encrypted five-segment JWT, and opaque reference token.",
          "heldState": "Issuer owns source claims; each output has its own exact artifact ID."
        },
        {
          "number": 2,
          "phase": "inspect",
          "action": "Let the holder decode JWS header/payload, inspect JWE envelope only, and view opaque bytes only.",
          "heldState": "Decoded JWS claims remain unverified; JWE plaintext is absent at holders without the decryption key."
        },
        {
          "number": 3,
          "phase": "validate",
          "action": "Route each artifact to its configured validation path.",
          "heldState": "Parsing creates no authenticated identity or access grant."
        },
        {
          "number": 4,
          "phase": "compare",
          "action": "Show protection and validator panels side by side.",
          "heldState": "JWT is a claims format; JWS gives integrity, JWE confidentiality/integrity; opaque is a client representation, not inherently weaker."
        }

      "negativeCases": [

        },

          "number": 2,
          "phase": "receive",
          "action": "API receives the exact compact token over the selected TLS carrier.",
          "heldState": "Inbox holds received bytes and untrusted decoded claims."

          "phase": "verify",
          "action": "Verify signature with configured key and algorithm.",
          "heldState": "A local signature-valid observation references the same token generation."

      "id": "JWT06",
      "title": "JWKS rotation and bounded refresh",
      "goal": "Teach availability and key rotation without inventing an RFC-mandated cache lifetime.",
      "actors": [
        "Issuer",
        "JWKS server",
        "Verifier cache",
        "Client"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Explicit demo policy: cache TTL 300s; one in-flight refresh per issuer; minimum 30s refresh interval; bounded negative cache; 2s fetch timeout; no stale-key acceptance after profile freshness limit. These are demo policies, not universal RFC/Kubernetes defaults."
      ],
      "steps": [
        {
          "number": 1,
          "phase": "overlap",
          "action": "Publish old+new public keys before issuing tokens with new kid.",
          "heldState": "Cache initially holds old key; issuer retains both signing generations during selected overlap."
        },
        {
          "number": 2,
          "phase": "refresh",
          "action": "Receive new kid; if refresh budget allows, perform one coalesced JWKS refresh.",
          "heldState": "Pending tokens stay unaccepted; requests share refresh work."
        },
        {
          "number": 3,
          "phase": "verify",
          "action": "Find new key, verify token and claims, then accept.",
          "heldState": "Cache revision and token key generation are explicit."
        },
        {
          "number": 4,
          "phase": "retire",
          "action": "After declared lifetime/overlap, retire old key and expire cache entries.",
          "heldState": "Retirement is not instantaneous universal token revocation."
        }
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "Unknown-kid flood is rate/capacity bounded.",
        "Refresh timeout/missing new kid denies that token; an unrelated valid cached-key token follows its own declared freshness policy."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Deterministic clock tests cover overlap, timeout and retry budget.",
        "Kubernetes-specific refresh internals must be checked against pinned implementation before claiming identical timings."
      ],

        {

          "phase": "login",

          "number": 2,
          "phase": "union",
          "action": "Gather matching RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding grants applicable to request scope.",
          "heldState": "Display contributing rules; there is no RBAC deny rule overriding another grant."
        },
        {
          "number": 3,
          "phase": "allow",
          "action": "Allow a request when at least one applicable matching rule grants it.",
          "heldState": "Store matched-grant explanation, not a guessed generic role label."

          "number": 4,
          "phase": "deny",

      "id": "MCP01",

      "actors": [
        "Host / MCP client C",
        "User and browser B",
        "Protected MCP resource R",
        "Authorization server A"
      ],
      "preconditions": [

        "Public desktop client is already registered at A; redirect is an approved loopback callback, no embedded client secret.",
        "A advertises S256; lab scope files:read is illustrative, not a standardized MCP-wide scope."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "C sends a self-contained tools/list POST with correct current-version metadata but no token; R returns 401 with Bearer resource_metadata and files:read guidance.",
        "C obtains and validates resource metadata, selects A, then separately obtains validated A metadata. Label discovery as configuration discovery, not authentication success.",
        "C creates per-attempt state, verifier and S256 challenge; B carries the authorization request with resource and requested scope to A.",
        "A performs its chosen user authentication and consent; depict those as A-owned local/interaction steps, not an MCP password exchange.",
        "B returns a short-lived code. C checks transaction/issuer/redirect binding, then sends grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, code, verifier and resource to the recorded token endpoint.",
        "After A validates the grant, C acquires an access token; C sends it in Authorization on the retried POST.",

      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Show token receipt before R validation and validation before tool execution.",
        "Verifier never appears in browser authorization parameters or at R.",
        "Resource parameter is visible on both authorization and token requests; access token is absent from URLs.",
        "Full and filtered replay converge on the same accepted-result state."

      "id": "MCP05",
      "title": "A received token is not yet an accepted request",

      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "C already holds a valid scoped token; no new login is needed.",
        "The lab host requires explicit approval for its synthetic destructive tool.",
        "The server has a separate per-object policy; this approval UI is a declared host policy, not a new OAuth grant."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "List tools under the authorization supplied on that request; show that a listed capability is not a promised successful mutation.",
        "The model proposes a tool call; C displays concrete tool/target/arguments for the host approval decision.",
        "If U declines, C sends no tools/call and retains the OAuth token unchanged.",
        "If U approves, C sends a fresh authenticated POST; R validates its authorization and P checks the chosen target.",
        "Return either a policy denial with no side effect or a completed operation result.",
        "Contrast AS sign-in/consent with this host approval and server authorization on separate cards."
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "Valid grant plus user denial; user approval plus ACL denial; untrusted tool annotations pretending an operation is harmless.",
        "Changed arguments after approval invalidate the declared host approval record.",
        "Self-asserted MCP clientInfo/capabilities cannot substitute for authentication.",
        "Cached tool list from another authorization context must not bypass the current request decision."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Expose independent booleans for tokenAccepted, hostInvocationApproved, resourceAuthorized and operationExecuted.",
        "Denied invocation creates no fictitious network exchange.",
        "No OIDC ID token or universal subject claim is invented merely because OAuth is used.",
        "Keyboard users can inspect the concrete operation and decline without losing journey focus."
      ],
      "sources": [
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools",
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9068.html",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html"
      ],
      "optional": false,
      "implementationPhase": "P5",
      "workspace": "mcp",
      "proposedRuntimeId": "lab-mcp08"
    },
    {
      "id": "MCP09",
      "title": "MCP proxy: a separate OAuth grant for the upstream API",
      "scope": "Optional deployment topology using core HTTP authorization on the MCP boundary and an independent upstream OAuth grant; not mandatory for every server.",
      "deliveryScope": "core",
      "goal": "Show both trust boundaries and the two different access tokens when an MCP server calls another protected service.",
      "actors": [
        "Client C",
        "User/browser B",
        "MCP proxy P",
        "MCP authorization server A",
        "Upstream authorization server UAS",
        "Upstream API U"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "C-to-P authorization already uses a token with P as resource.",
        "P is separately registered as an OAuth client at UAS; no upstream token is initially available.",
        "Use two collapsed chapters so only one authorization boundary is expanded at a time."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "P accepts C authorization for the requested MCP operation, then discovers that upstream access is absent.",
        "P binds an upstream authorization transaction to the initiating user/client/operation and obtains the required consent.",
        "B authorizes at UAS; P redeems that upstream code using its own registered client configuration.",
        "P stores the separately issued upstream token with its own audience, issuer and grant record.",
        "P calls U with that token; U independently validates and authorizes the requested API operation.",
        "P accepts the upstream result and returns the permitted MCP result to C without exposing upstream credentials."
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "Upstream consent denied; upstream token expired; U rejects its audience or ACL.",
        "The C token cannot fill the missing upstream-token slot.",
        "One user/client grant must not be reused as another user/client grant.",
        "If a product instead uses token exchange, it requires a separately sourced extension profile; do not silently claim it happened here."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Two exact token IDs, two intended resources and two authorization contexts remain visible.",
        "P receiving the U response is distinct from interpreting its accepted result.",
        "Failure of the upstream hop does not retroactively invalidate the accepted C-to-P token.",
        "No password/code/token is collected by ordinary tool arguments or leaked into tool output."
      ],
      "sources": [
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations",
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/security_best_practices",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8707.html",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7636.html",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750.html"
      ],
      "optional": false,
      "implementationPhase": "P5",
      "workspace": "mcp",
      "proposedRuntimeId": "lab-mcp09"
    },
    {
      "id": "MCP10",
      "title": "Proxy consent cannot be inherited by a different MCP client",
      "scope": "Optional proxy topology with required consent isolation for the depicted clients. Historical DCR attack context is deprecated compatibility, not a recommended onboarding default.",
      "deliveryScope": "core",
      "goal": "Demonstrate the confused-deputy boundary with an existing upstream login/consent cookie and a newly introduced downstream client.",
      "actors": [
        "User/browser B",
        "Previously approved client C1",
        "New client C2",
        "MCP proxy P",
        "Upstream authorization server UAS"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "P uses one registered upstream client ID; B already has an upstream consent cookie.",
        "C1 is approved for this user; C2 is not.",
        "The historically documented attack can use DCR; the core lesson is consent isolation, not a recommendation to deploy deprecated registration."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "Show the prior C1 approval record and upstream browser cookie as separate artifacts.",
        "C2 requests proxy access with its own registered redirect and requested upstream permission set.",
        "P checks the user/client-specific consent record before starting the upstream authorization attempt.",
        "P presents C2 identity, target redirect hostname and requested upstream access; refusal ends the attempt.",
        "Only explicit approval creates the C2 consent record; any upstream automatic sign-in/consent behavior cannot create that record on its own.",
        "Bind callback/state and the resulting grant to the approved C2 transaction."
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "A global user-has-consented flag, C1 cookie replay, mismatched redirect, CSRF token mismatch or tampered consent record.",
        "A display name resembling C1 is not an identity match.",
        "An upstream consent cookie must not produce a downstream code for an unapproved client."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "The default safe path blocks before contacting UAS when consent is absent/denied.",
        "No real malicious redirect is opened; the attack input is a frozen synthetic fixture.",
        "Tests assert zero downstream authorization/code release before matching consent.",
        "Explain exactly which approval must be renewed, avoiding a generic login failed message."
      ],
      "sources": [
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/security_best_practices",
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations",
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html"
      ],
      "optional": false,
      "implementationPhase": "P5",
      "workspace": "mcp",
      "proposedRuntimeId": "lab-mcp10"
    },
    {
      "id": "MCP11",
      "title": "Reject token passthrough across the proxy boundary",
      "scope": "Core MCP 2026-07-28 HTTP authorization teaching profile; authorization itself is optional for MCP deployments. No deprecated session or DCR default.",
      "deliveryScope": "core",
      "goal": "Make wrong-recipient token acceptance and downstream forwarding visibly separate forbidden transitions.",
      "actors": [
        "Client C",
        "MCP proxy P",
        "Upstream API U",
        "Their respective authorization servers"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "A synthetic upstream token is valid for U but not P.",
        "A separate valid P token and separately issued U token are available for the corrected comparison.",
        "No permissive broken path is presented as a selectable production configuration."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "C presents the U token to P as if it authorized MCP access.",
        "P receives and inspects the token, rejects the intended-recipient check and returns an invalid-token response.",
        "The blocked route to U remains visibly inactive; there is no token forwarding or upstream side effect.",
        "Switch to the corrected comparison: P accepts its own resource token.",
        "P obtains/selects the separate U token under MCP09 and uses only that token for U.",
        "Display the two validation records and the rejected token history without promoting rejected possession to authority."
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "JWT with wrong aud, opaque token whose authoritative metadata identifies U, or a token from an unrelated issuer.",
        "Valid P token forwarded unchanged to U is also disallowed.",
        "No fallback forwards an unrecognized token merely because P cannot parse it."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Assert U receives no request in the rejected attempt.",
        "Incoming/outgoing token object identities differ in the successful proxy path.",
        "A user-readable token error does not echo secret token bytes.",
        "Audience rejection remains correct with matching scope names at P and U."
      ],
      "sources": [
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8707.html",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9068.html",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7662.html"
      ],
      "optional": false,
      "implementationPhase": "P5",
      "workspace": "mcp",
      "proposedRuntimeId": "lab-mcp11"
    },
    {
      "id": "MCP12",
      "title": "Untrusted discovery URLs and metadata do not trigger unsafe fetches",
      "scope": "Core authorization security demonstrated with fixed offline fixtures; deployment-specific network allowlists are explicit local policy.",
      "deliveryScope": "core",
      "goal": "Teach metadata and authorization-URL validation with an offline simulation of redirects, DNS results and credential destinations.",
      "actors": [
        "Client C or metadata-fetching AS",
        "Synthetic metadata source M",
        "Synthetic policy/egress gate G"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Fixed input fixtures include a legitimate public URL, private/link-local targets, redirect chains and changed DNS answers.",
        "The shipping learning app performs no actual discovery/token/authorization fetch from user-provided values.",
        "Enterprise private-network exceptions, if shown, are explicit administrator allowlists rather than universal unsafe exceptions."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "Receive a metadata/authorization/CIMD URL as untrusted input.",
        "Validate scheme, authority and deployment policy before any simulated request; separately evaluate each redirected/resolved destination.",
        "Model bounded response size/time, trusted TLS identity and metadata schema/resource/issuer checks.",
        "At a denied destination, stop before a simulated credential-bearing POST or browser navigation.",
        "Show that accepted metadata still grants no user access and cannot transfer an existing issuer credential to a new issuer.",
        "Render the reason and a redacted diagnostic event; retain no real URL query secret."
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "javascript/data/file authorization URL; HTTPS URL redirecting to loopback/link-local; DNS rebinding; invalid TLS identity.",
        "Poisoned token_endpoint; resource_metadata naming a different resource; CIMD mismatch.",
        "A same-hostname but different issuer path attempts credential reuse.",
        "Oversized or cyclic metadata/redirect chain exhausts a bounded budget."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "Network interception tests observe zero external application requests in source HTTP, standalone HTTP and file modes.",
        "Assertions distinguish blocked-before-send from rejected-after-response.",
        "Document model policy versus normative requirements; a private enterprise AS is not universally forbidden by MCP.",
        "Source links are explicit user navigation, never automatic page-load fetches or OAuth launches."
      ],
      "sources": [
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9728.html",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414.html",
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations",
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/security_best_practices",
        "https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00"
      ],
      "optional": false,
      "implementationPhase": "P5",
      "workspace": "mcp",
      "proposedRuntimeId": "lab-mcp12"
    },
    {
      "id": "MCP13",
      "title": "Local stdio: process credentials and OS authority",
      "scope": "Core stdio transport, outside the MCP HTTP OAuth authorization mechanism. Environment/secret-provider and OS policy are declared local deployment behavior.",
      "deliveryScope": "core",
      "goal": "Explain why local subprocess access follows process/credential boundaries rather than the remote HTTP OAuth challenge.",
      "actors": [
        "Host C",
        "Local MCP subprocess S",
        "OS credential store / launcher O",
        "Optional upstream API U"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "MCP 2026-07-28 stdio transport; a restricted synthetic process profile.",
        "S receives only its configured credential via its declared launcher/secret-provider path.",
        "No real subprocess, OS secret or network access is performed by the simulator."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "C launches the modeled subprocess under the selected OS identity and restricted environment.",
        "O supplies the per-server credential; label the provider action and resulting local possession.",
        "C and S exchange newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout; do not insert an HTTP 401/WWW-Authenticate flow.",
        "S attempts a local resource action under OS policy or uses its separately obtained upstream credential.",
        "An OS/resource policy decision determines the operation result; MCP transport alone does not sandbox S.",
        "On termination show the modeled credential cleanup separately from upstream token validity/revocation."
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "Missing environment/secret-provider value; OS file denial; missing upstream scope.",
        "A global inherited credential would be overbroad; use a visible bad-configuration fixture, not the default.",
        "HTTP-to-stdio proxy would introduce a remote boundary requiring its own declared protection.",
        "MCP roots or tool approval are not an OS containment guarantee."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "No browser authorization grant appears unless a separately selected upstream library actually uses one.",
        "Local identity, token authority and allowed file access stay independent.",
        "Cross-link workstation/PAM/LSM material instead of inventing platform behavior here.",
        "Diagnostics never print environment values or inherited real file paths."
      ],
      "sources": [
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio",
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/tutorials/security/local-server-security",
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization"
      ],
      "optional": false,
      "implementationPhase": "P5",
      "workspace": "mcp",
      "proposedRuntimeId": "lab-mcp13"
    },
    {
      "id": "MCP14",
      "title": "Optional machine client: client-credentials extension",
      "scope": "Optional io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials extension, explicitly enabled and version/snapshot-pinned; not a core mandatory user authorization flow.",
      "deliveryScope": "optional",
      "goal": "Show an application obtaining its own authorization without pretending to be an interactively authenticated user.",
      "actors": [
        "Confidential machine client C",
        "Authorization server A",
        "MCP resource R"
      ],
      "preconditions": [
        "Explicitly enabled io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials extension and compatible client/server policy.",
        "Pre-registered confidential client; choose private_key_jwt authentication or a secret-based comparison.",
        "Current extension source must be pinned by snapshot/hash at implementation freeze; no made-up extension version."
      ],
      "steps": [
        "C declares extension support through the current per-request capabilities profile.",
        "C creates a short-lived signed client assertion, or selects its securely configured secret-based authentication method.",
        "C requests grant_type=client_credentials with the intended resource and application scopes at A.",
        "A validates client authentication and application policy, then issues an access token for R.",
        "C sends a version-correct authenticated POST; R validates the token and authorizes the machine operation.",
        "At expiry, C obtains another client-credentials token; do not fabricate a browser or assume refresh_token grant support."
      ],
      "negativeCases": [
        "Extension unsupported or policy disallows machine access.",
        "Bad assertion signature/audience/expiry, reused jti under the selected replay-protection profile, or invalid secret.",
        "Valid client authentication but requested application scope denied.",
        "Machine token must not inherit a human subject or an existing user consent record."
      ],
      "acceptance": [
        "JWT assertion, private key and resulting access token have separate identities and holder permissions.",
        "Private signing key never leaves C; assertion is delivered to A, not used as R bearer token.",
        "No mandatory-core label, interactive consent event or guaranteed refresh token.",
        "Cross-link JWT client-assertion validation; do not mislabel client authentication as JWT bearer authorization grant."
      ],
      "sources": [
        "https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/auth/oauth-client-credentials",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749.html#section-4.4",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7523.html",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8707.html",
        "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750.html"
      ],
      "optional": true,
      "implementationPhase": "P5",
      "workspace": "mcp",
      "proposedRuntimeId": "lab-mcp14"
    }
  ],

          "id": "admission-write",
